chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Zarif ibn Nasih, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

If a man fasts for part of the month of Ramadan and remains ill until he dies, there is no obligation upon him [to make up the fasts]. And if he recovered [from illness] then became ill again until he died, and he had wealth, charity is given on his behalf; and if he had no wealth, his heir gives charity on his behalf.

key_terms.تُصَدِّقَ عَنْهُ: Charity is given on his behalf
key_terms.فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ: There is no obligation upon him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for making up missed Ramadan fasts if a person dies while ill?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between temporary illness and persistent incapacity in Ramadan jurisprudence, establishing that death while ill exempts one from *qada* (making up fasts) but requires *fidyah* (charity) if recovery occurred prior to death. The ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the deceased's estate or heir fulfilling the financial obligation when the individual could not complete the act themselves, reflecting the principle of *khulaf'* (successors) in ritual duties.
